evals.prompt: A NixOS module currently configures `virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.lab.image`, but the requirement is a native NixOS container with `privateNetwork`, a writable `/dev/bus/usb` bind mount, and OpenSSH enabled inside the guest. Explain the correction and provide the module fragment.
evals.expected_output: Uses `containers.lab`, native bindMounts, and nested container config; removes OCI image and backend-specific device options.
expectations: Chooses the native NixOS container namespace rather than OCI
Represents the USB bind mount with hostPath and isReadOnly false
Enables OpenSSH inside the container config

evals.prompt: Fix a NixOS service module whose evaluator provides only `lib.mkEnableOption`, `lib.mkOption`, `lib.mkIf`, `lib.types.package`, `lib.types.port`, `lib.types.str`, and `lib.types.listOf`. It needs configurable package, port, and extra arguments, a systemd service, and a firewall port. Describe how you will avoid relying on unavailable helpers and how you will test non-default values.
evals.expected_output: Treats the supplied fake lib as the API, uses only available helpers or builtins, flows all service values through cfg, and proposes enabled/disabled alternate-value evaluation.
expectations: Does not assume general nixpkgs.lib helpers are present
Uses cfg values in ExecStart and the firewall definition
Tests at least one non-default configuration and the disabled case

evals.prompt: Review this Home Manager-style fragment: `xdg.portal.extraPortals = config.xdg.portal.extraPortals ++ [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland ];`. The module must preserve portal contributions from other desktops and add Hyprland plus a non-Hyprland fallback only when Hyprland is enabled. Give a corrected pattern and explain the recursion risk.
evals.expected_output: Uses module merging such as mkAfter instead of reading an option while defining it, gates the contribution with mkIf, and preserves non-Hyprland defaults.
expectations: Identifies self-reference while defining the same option
Uses module merge priority/order combinators
Preserves existing portal packages and fallback defaults

evals.prompt: Package a small C CLI with `stdenv.mkDerivation`. Its source is pinned on GitHub; the build uses `make PREFIX=$out`; shell completions use `installShellFiles`; tests must run; the binary must land in `$out/bin`; and callers depend on `meta.mainProgram`. State the important derivation fields and the checks you would run.
evals.expected_output: Places installShellFiles in nativeBuildInputs, pins source/hash, preserves make/check/install contracts and meta, and distinguishes evaluation from an actual build.
expectations: Classifies installShellFiles as a native build tool
Includes fixed source identity, checks, install destination, and mainProgram
Runs both an evaluation-level check and a build-level check

evals.prompt: A `buildRustPackage` enables `download-binaries`; its `build.rs` downloads ONNX Runtime and a model with curl. Rewrite the packaging strategy so sandboxed builds remain offline. The model should remain inspectable through passthru.
evals.expected_output: Disables the download feature, uses an ONNX Runtime package in buildInputs, fetches the model as a fixed Nix input, passes store paths to the build, exposes passthru.assets.model, and does not weaken sandboxing.
expectations: Moves every network artifact into a fixed-output Nix fetch
Uses store paths and a system dependency during the build
Rejects curl/wget and sandbox-disabling workarounds

evals.prompt: A systemd script embedded in an indented Nix string must pass the literal shell expression `${PORT}` to runtime and construct a Nix path for `configDir/app.toml`. Show the two correct forms and explain what layer expands each.
evals.expected_output: Uses `''${PORT}` for literal shell interpolation and path addition for the child path, clearly distinguishing Nix evaluation from shell runtime.
expectations: Escapes the shell interpolation from Nix
Uses path composition rather than accidental string interpolation
Explains the evaluation layer for each expression

evals.prompt: Write a concise issue handoff for an observed NixOS option-does-not-exist error. The exact rebuild command, system, release, nixpkgs revision, stale option path, and likely replacement are known, but the replacement has not yet been evaluated. Separate evidence from hypothesis.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the failure as evaluation, includes exact reproduction and provenance, records the stale path as observed, labels the replacement as likely/unverified, and avoids claiming a confirmed root cause.
expectations: Includes command, platform/release/revision, expected versus actual, and log evidence
Separates observed facts, likely fix, and unverified items
Does not overclaim runtime or confirmed-root-cause evidence

evals.prompt: A flake input exports `packages.aarch64-darwin.release` but no `packages.aarch64-darwin.default`. The current flake references `.default` and fails. Explain the safe repair workflow and the validation commands.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the actual input outputs, selects the existing release attribute for the intended system, and validates flake output shape before building the exact installable.
expectations: Does not invent or assume a default package
Keeps the target system explicit
Separates flake evaluation/show/check from a concrete build
